# synthetic-sciences/openscience — pinned source assessment

**Source:** [`synthetic-sciences/openscience` at `4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/commit/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5) (2026-09-23, `release: v2.0.130`). The ignored local working copy is `references/work/openscience/`. It is an external technique source, not evidence of Google's private Co-Scientist implementation, and cannot become a runtime dependency.

## Terms and source boundary

The pinned root [LICENSE](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/LICENSE) and package metadata declare Apache-2.0 for OpenScience's own code. Its [NOTICE](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/NOTICE) identifies separately licensed bundled material, including K-Dense and other skill collections, Anthropic document skills under Anthropic's terms, an NVIDIA BioNeMo-derived skill with CC-BY-4.0/Apache components, MIT-licensed icons and helpers, and OFL fonts. The source has 5,883 tracked files; 3,406 are under `backend/`, 2,229 under `frontend/`, and a large share are bundled skills/assets rather than the request runtime. Eight tracked root or component license/notice files were located. No source, prompt, skill, asset, or dependency has been copied into Co-Scientist, and no upstream setup or agent workflow has been run. Any selected component must be checked against its own license and attributed in the maintained destination.

The pinned [architecture document](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/ARCHITECTURE.md) describes a Bun/TypeScript local server with a SolidJS browser workspace and CLI, backed by local sessions, tools, model providers, and optional remote compute. Its [security document](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/SECURITY.md) says the service binds to localhost, uses Host/Origin checks, and offers an optional bearer token; project selectors are not tenant isolation. Its own architecture says request receipts precede model execution, identical request IDs replay one run, changed content conflicts, and terminal receipts outlive a bounded event journal. These are documentation claims to compare against implementation and tests before treating them as mechanisms. The same document says a process crash interrupts external work rather than automatically replaying effects, and live permission continuations are not restored across crashes. Those boundaries differ from our hosted owner-scoped FastAPI and durable task recovery.

OpenScience can route through user credentials, local providers, or its managed paid Ace service; compute can involve user-owned remote resources. This campaign will not run its setup, agents, paid model routes, or remote compute. The candidate surface is existing Co-Scientist API/React workflows, never a second Bun server or workbench.

## Inventory and inspection boundary

The tracked tree contains 5,883 files, including 876 paths matching test/spec conventions (595 backend, 267 frontend, 14 tooling). The core runtime is concentrated in [`backend/cli/src/runtime/{runs,events,decisions}.ts`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/tree/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/runtime), with related session, server, tool, provider and permission modules; the browser workspace is under `frontend/workspace/src/`. There are model- and role-specific prompt files under [`backend/cli/src/agent/prompt/`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/tree/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/agent/prompt), including `science.txt`, `explore.txt`, `specialist.txt`, and generic provider prompts. These are source prompts, not evidence that their advertised behavior is effective or Google-backed.

The inspected root `package.json` runs `bun run tooling/repo/setup.ts` for setup and invokes a UI build, model-catalog fetch, and native compilation for release. None of those scripts was executed. The architecture says generated assets and model snapshots are gitignored and created by setup/build scripts, so a source-only inspection must not mistake missing generated files for missing product behavior. The source's [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/SECURITY.md) states that trace sharing may include prompts, reasoning, tool inputs/outputs, and usage when signed in, and that it is governed by consent and redaction. That trace-export policy is not a pattern to import into Co-Scientist's owner-scoped evidence and logging without a separate privacy acceptance case.

## Current Co-Scientist boundary for comparison

The **Google-backed requirement** boundary remains the existing multi-agent hypothesis workflow, Elo comparison, scientific evidence and report outputs; the runtime and workbench details below are **local design choices** that preserve durable recovery and authenticated ownership. The user authorized improvements within them, not a new execution runtime.

Our [`POST /api/runs` creation](../../app/app/runs_crud.py) persists a new UUID draft after credential and document validation; [`POST /start`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py) reserves owner capacity and queues its durable workflow. Task rows have unique `(run_id, idempotency_key)` and lease-owner checks ([`store/tasks.py`](../../app/app/store/tasks.py)), but creation has no client-supplied request ID. A lost create response can therefore make a retry create another draft. This is a concrete candidate gap at the owned API and browser create flow, subject to checking OpenScience's implemented receipt and conflict semantics before design.

Cancellation revokes queued/leased tasks, updates the run and appends a terminal event. The worker heartbeat stops a revoked coroutine, and node execution checks run status before committing a checkpoint. Those guards exist; the interval between that check and the checkpoint/successor transaction needs a targeted race audit before it is called a defect ([`runs_lifecycle.py`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py), [`engine_tasks.py`](../../app/app/engine_tasks.py)).

The owned [`/api/runs/{id}/events?after=<seq>` stream](../../app/app/runs_events.py) replays the persisted per-run sequence and tails new events behind the same ownership middleware. The React [`use_run_stream` hook](../../app/frontend/src/hooks/use_run_stream.ts) reconnects and deduplicates by sequence. It does not require a separate bounded event journal. Owner-scoped collection routes already expose hypotheses, evidence, reviews, citations, reports and metrics; public shares pass publication gates and omit private attachment text. Task provenance and dependency fields are stored, but the task diagnostics payload exposes only status/error/attempt data ([`runs_collections.py`](../../app/app/runs_collections.py)). Whether richer artifact visibility improves an existing screen requires a concrete user flow.

The current [`/status` endpoint](../../app/app/diagnostics_api.py) probes configured literature/web connectors and presents capability availability to the composer; it does not advertise multiple execution runtimes, because [`select_provider`](../../app/app/engine_adapter/provider.py) always chooses the existing engine. Importing OpenScience's Bun server or treating a localhost project selector as tenant isolation would conflict with our owner-scoped FastAPI and SQLite task model. Its provider and capability designs can only be considered as adapters or better disclosure inside the existing stack.

## Pinned mechanism and test map

This is an inspection of shipped source and its tests, not a claim that upstream tests passed here. The `session` tree holds prompt input, research-loop, checkpoint, restart, trace, and tool-outcome modules; the receipt and replay contract is in the runtime layer adjacent to it. The existing workbench's local-server lifecycle is documented in [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/ARCHITECTURE.md#L11-L42). The relevant source map is:

| Concern | Implemented mechanism and test evidence | Operational boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run admission | [`RuntimeRuns.admit`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/runtime/runs.ts#L180-L295) fingerprints input, locks a local session, persists an identity receipt before model work, replays exact retries and conflicts on changed content. [Tests](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/runtime/runtime-runs.test.ts#L58-L150) cover eight concurrent submissions, changed input, receipt survival and interrupted crash recovery. | The implementation joins a new prompt to an active session run; that is its chat behavior, not Co-Scientist's run semantics. Its cross-process lease is for a local data root. |
| Events and reconnect | [`runtime` routes](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/server/routes/runtime.ts#L51-L77) advertise capabilities, receipts and a cursor snapshot. The [SSE route](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/server/routes/runtime.ts#L190-L385) subscribes before replay, deduplicates the handoff, accepts `Last-Event-ID`, emits heartbeats and signals an expired/future cursor. [Tests](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/runtime/runtime-events.test.ts#L663-L845) exercise those boundaries. | Its 2,048-event journal can expire; our SQLite event log is append-only and owned. A different cursor protocol is not itself a user improvement. |
| Permissions and decisions | [`PermissionNext`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/permission/next.ts#L83-L253) applies deny-first local policy with once/session/project/global grants ([tests](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/permission/next.test.ts)). [`RuntimeDecisions.decide`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/runtime/decisions.ts#L72-L133) persists a decision receipt before applying its live continuation and rejects conflicts ([tests](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/runtime/runtime-decisions.test.ts#L23-L150)). | Its project selector is not hosted tenant isolation; a crashed process cannot restore an in-memory approval continuation. |
| Artifacts and lineage | [`ArtifactStore`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/artifact/store.ts#L19-L95) records immutable saved versions with SHA-256/size and execution metadata ([version test](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/tool/artifact-save-file.test.ts#L51-L99)). The [small-scale JSON provenance graph](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/science/provenance/store.ts#L1-L11) stores typed content-derived nodes and edges, with project-scoped trace/export [tests](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/server/provenance.test.ts#L51-L246). | A workspace file becomes a result only after an explicit save; the JSON graph is not a replacement for our append-only SQLite lineage. |
| Providers | [`ModelsDev`](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/provider/models.ts#L36-L235) validates cached/live model metadata for reasoning, tools, limits and listed cost ([schema test](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/provider/provider.test.ts#L117-L142)). [Managed gateway calls](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/src/provider/provider.ts#L891-L990) use an idempotency key and distinguish conflicts, sealed outcomes and post-dispatch uncertainty ([tests](https://github.com/synthetic-sciences/openscience/blob/4e060d6c3670e3704f34b5cb6fe49ef8fafb29f5/backend/cli/test/provider/managed-conflict.test.ts#L166-L225)). | Metadata is not a live compatibility or zero-price check. Replay guarantees depend on its managed gateway, not direct BYOK providers. Managed Ace and optional remote compute are outside this campaign's spending boundary. |

## Candidate register

All findings here are **external techniques** or **local design choices**, not new Google-backed requirements. No candidate is adopted merely because upstream ships it. No model calls, upstream code execution, paid tools, or new dependencies are needed for this source audit.

| ID | Concrete gap or disposition question | Acceptance boundary and current state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M8-ADM-01 | A lost `POST /api/runs` response can induce a second owned draft because each call gets a new UUID; queue idempotency begins only after the run exists. | Open: compare a client-supplied request ID plus canonical payload receipt. Identical owned retries, including concurrent ones, must return one run; changed content under the same key must conflict; another owner must not see or bind the receipt. Keep existing unkeyed clients compatible. Test the API and browser retry boundary without inference. Adapt the contract, do not copy its local-file lease. |
| M8-CAN-02 | A cancel could complete between the worker's post-node status check and checkpoint/successor commit. | Adopted locally: deterministic API/task races now reject post-cancel checkpoint and successor writes under the current task lease and run status. This is a correctness change, not a scientific-quality claim; release remains open. |
| M8-CAN-03 | Initial run admission had a cancel race after capacity reservation but before bootstrap enqueue; bootstrap could read status before cancel and then overwrite `CANCELLED` with `RUNNING`. | Adopted locally: atomic start/cancel transactions and lease-fenced bootstrap/safety status transitions pass owned API/task races, normal start, restart, and rollback tests. No inference or new runtime. Release remains open. |
| M8-PAUSE-04 | A pause may complete after a node's status refresh but before a normal successor transaction. The cancellation guard allows paused runs because the paused-checkpoint path must still commit. | Open, discovered during M8-CAN-02 review: reproduce at the durable API boundary and preserve a resumable paused checkpoint without new claimable successor work. Do not treat pause as cancellation or break existing recovery. No inference. |
| M8-CAN-05 | Final report publication may race with cancellation after the finalizer's earlier status checks. | Adopted local correctness fix, code commit `daa048cf`: a claimed finalizer now atomically validates its lease and publishes report, facts, events, status and notification; startup settles a crash-orphaned finalizer after committed publication. Owned API and recovery tests pass. Release remains open; no inference. |
| M8-CAN-05b | A stale finalizer can overwrite cancellation with an empty-leaderboard block or append a final-safety allow/redact event after lease loss. | Adopted local correctness fix, code commit `1456850d`: final safety decision/event and readiness block writes now require the claimed finalize lease and commit atomically. Owned cancellation races, valid block/redaction and authenticated event replay pass. M8 release remains open; no inference. |
| M8-CAN-05c | The separate monitor-halt finalizer path invoked a legacy safety gate without the claimed task; cancellation could therefore be followed by its audit row or safety event even though a later status guard prevented a status reversal. | Adopted local consistency fix, code commit `fb090375`: the halt gate receives the claimed finalizer and uses the existing atomic lease-fenced decision/event/status transaction. Owned cancellation race and valid halt audit/event-order tests pass. This is not a reported security vulnerability or Google-backed requirement; M8 release remains open. No inference. |
| M8-PAUSE-08e | A `/pause` accepted during final drain could be overwritten by the finalizer's later unconditional `SYNTHESIZING` update, allowing publication before explicit resume. An early stale PAUSED read could also write a paused checkpoint after `/resume` had queued continuation. | Adopted local correctness fix, code commit `cdc5fd19`: lease-fenced pause-or-synthesize transaction and atomic early pause recheck preserve the winning lifecycle; owner API races, restart, explicit resume, artifact visibility and event order pass. M8 release remains open. No inference. |
| M8-RES-06 | A final-safety-blocked run can retain a checkpoint pointing to an already-completed finalize task; direct `/resume` reported queued with no claimable work. | Adopted local correctness fix: direct resume returns 409 before mutating status, event or task state. An owner API regression exercises a real succeeded finalizer and final safety block; ordinary failed and paused recovery still passes. No inference. |
| M8-SAF-07 | A stale bootstrap intake verdict recorded a safety decision/event or redacted the goal after the lease was lost, even though its status transition was fenced. | Adopted local correctness fix: the current unexpired bootstrap lease now guards the decision, redaction, safety event and stop status in one transaction. Owned cancellation/expiry/reassignment tests, valid provenance and report redaction pass. No inference. |
| M8-SSE-03 | OpenScience has explicit snapshot/gap and SSE ID semantics. | Compare our owner-scoped append-only sequence replay and React reconnect; accept only a demonstrated lost/duplicated event or poor recovery. Avoid transplanting a bounded journal for its own sake. |
| M8-DEC-04 | Scoped interactive approval and decision receipts could affect safety review. | Compare our persisted review and safety gates; local project/global grants cannot replace authenticated ownership, and in-memory continuation would weaken crash recovery. No adoption absent a specific safe user flow. |
| M8-ART-05 | Immutable result versions and a browsable lineage graph may improve result interpretation. | Compare existing append-only hypothesis/evidence/report provenance and artifact UI; accept only a concrete visibility or integrity gap in an existing flow. Do not install a second artifact store. |
| M8-CAP-06 | A richer model/provider catalog may disclose capability mismatches earlier. | Compare `/status`, free-model qualification and actual interface probes. Listed cost or ability alone is not verified zero price or tool/stream compatibility. No catalog fetch or managed paid route for this assessment. |
| M8-LLM-07 | Provider post-dispatch timeouts can have an unknown outcome that should not be assumed safe to replay. | Audit the existing LLM request/retry boundary and provider support. Accept a change only if it demonstrably prevents duplicate/charged dispatch or preserves a durable unknown state without breaking bounded free fallbacks or explicit BYOK behavior. No live inference needed for the initial audit. |

The source also includes a generic chat workspace, session follow-up joining, remote compute, shareable traces, and a separate agent/provider runtime. Those are outside the authorized improvement surface.

## Local comparison and decisions

| ID | Local counterpart and decision | Verification, cost and reuse |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M8-ADM-01 | **Accepted reliability improvement.** [`runs_crud.create_run`](../../app/app/runs_crud.py) resolves owned documents and credentials, then [`store.create_run`](../../app/app/store/runs.py) generates a fresh UUID. The frontend's [`createRun`](../../app/frontend/src/api/runs.ts) carries no retry identity, and the create/start UI resets to an editable draft on a failed request. Internal `(run_id, idempotency_key)` task uniqueness cannot deduplicate two run rows. | Independently implement an owned, canonical request receipt at the FastAPI/SQLite boundary; preserve unkeyed clients and explicit BYOK. Red API tests must show one run for concurrent exact retries, 409 for changed input, owner isolation, and no incomplete receipt after a setup failure. The browser must reuse a pending identity across ambiguous retry/refresh, then clear it on successful start. No model call is needed for tests. A new persistent table requires a consistent production backup before deployment. Do not copy OpenScience's local lease or session-follow-up behavior. |
| M8-CAN-02 | **Accepted correctness improvement.** The worker's [`execute_node_task`](../../app/app/engine_tasks.py) rechecks status after node execution, but cancellation revokes tasks and updates the run in separate transactions ([`runs_lifecycle`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py), [`tasks_lifecycle`](../../app/app/store/tasks_lifecycle.py)). The subsequent [`_save_state_and_enqueue`](../../app/app/engine_tasks_support.py) transaction checks checkpoint sequence, not whether its lease was revoked. Thus a completed cancel can precede a new checkpoint and queued successor. | Independently implement a commit-time lease/run guard inside the same SQLite write transaction as checkpoint and successor. Red test must force cancel after the node's last status check and before commit, through the owned API and durable execution boundary; no post-cancel checkpoint/successor may appear. Test pause/resume and normal commits for regression. No inference or new dependency. |
| M8-CAN-03 | **Adopted local correctness improvement.** [`start_run`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py) formerly reserved capacity, emitted an event, and enqueued bootstrap in separate transactions; cancellation could land between them or bootstrap could later overwrite `CANCELLED`. | The owned API/task tests reproduce the races. [`runs_admission`](../../app/app/store/runs_admission.py) now reserves capacity in the same transaction as bootstrap task and queued event; cancel revokes tasks and writes status/event atomically; [`runs_bootstrap`](../../app/app/store/runs_bootstrap.py) and the intake status gate require a live bootstrap lease. No upstream code was copied, no model call or new dependency. Full release/deployment verification remains open. |
| M8-RES-06 | **Adopted local correctness fix.** A completed final safety block can leave `resume_successor=engine.finalize` pointing to a succeeded finalize row. Direct `/resume` reused it and falsely reported queued. | [`runs_lifecycle.resume_run`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py) now rejects `BLOCKED` before admission, matching `/start`. The red-then-green owner API test in [`test_resume_final_safety_block.py`](../../app/tests/test_resume_final_safety_block.py) runs the finalizer, verifies the succeeded task and safety block, then checks 409, owner isolation, unchanged status/tasks and ordered replay. Fifteen focused tests include ordinary paused/failed recovery; four size tests, Ruff, mypy and diff checks pass. No model call, copied code or new dependency. Release remains open. |
| M8-SAF-07 | **Adopted local correctness fix.** Intake block/hold status and event were lease-fenced, but [`apply_safety_gate`](../../app/app/safety_gate.py) recorded the decision, emitted `safety.intake`, and could redact the goal before that guard. | The red owner API/bootstrap test observed post-cancel redaction and event; the gate now verifies the current unexpired bootstrap lease in the same transaction as every verdict effect. Cancellation, expiry, reassignment, valid redaction and final safety tests pass. No copied code, inference or new dependency; release remains open. |
| M8-PAUSE-04 | **Adopted local reliability improvement.** The stale status snapshot let a specialist node enqueue a successor after completed pause; separate pause transactions also left a write window between queued-task revocation and PAUSED status. | Code commit `a62a5cbf` makes the owned pause API transaction atomic and selects the paused checkpoint under the node's commit transaction. Red/green owned API/task tests cover both interleavings, no claimable successor, checkpoint/metrics/event, lease ownership and explicit resume. No upstream code, dependency or model call. Full release remains open. |
| M8-PAUSE-08a | **Adopted local reliability improvement.** An already-leased fan-out scheduler or aggregate can commit queued work after `/pause`; [`claim_task`](../../app/app/store/tasks.py) previously ignored the run's PAUSED state, while [`enqueue_run_workflow`](../../app/app/task_worker_enqueue.py) could miss that work and enqueue a competing fallback. | Code commit `9aa8fbc1` fences engine claims under the queue write lock and serializes unpause, checkpoint/task discovery, writer revival and fallback enqueue. Red/green owned API/task tests cover generation, shared review/verification/reflection scheduler, verification aggregate, paused/expired writers and a checkpoint-commit race. No upstream code, dependency or inference; full release remains open. |
| M8-PAUSE-08b | **Adopted local reliability improvement.** A sole pre-checkpoint bootstrap can remain leased when `/pause` returns, or its exhausted lease can be abandoned to FAILED while the run stays PAUSED; neither shape had a checkpoint or paused task for [`_is_resumable`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py). | Code commit `69df1a79` lets a live or specifically abandoned bootstrap resume on its original task row and moves pause/successor choice into the bootstrap checkpoint transaction. Red/green owned API/task tests cover stale status, lease abandonment, permanent failure, intake audit, ownership and cancellation. No upstream code or inference; full M8 release remains open. |
| M8-PAUSE-08c | **Adopted local event-order correction; ranking continuation already covered.** A late ranking match/finalize commit leaves a queued successor, but M8-PAUSE-08a's run-status claim fence keeps it unclaimable until resume. The match progress emitter previously wrote a `running` event after `pause_requested`. | Code commit `47e071ae` serializes progress-event admission with `/pause`. Owned API/task tests verify persisted match details/Elo, finalizer metrics, checkpoint/provenance, unclaimability while paused and exact successor claim after resume. The finalizer's truthful completion event remains. No upstream code or inference; full M8 release remains open. |
| M8-PAUSE-08d | **Adopted and locally closed; M8 release open.** Distinct family checks initially missed cancel/resume admission, paused restart and whole-run claim/event continuity. | 08d1 makes cancellation terminal across resume admission; 08d2 verifies restart and exact checkpoint-linked recovery; 08d3 drives owned pause across a late leased-node commit, proves its queued successor unclaimable, then reuses that sole continuation on resume with ordered events. Existing bootstrap, fan-out, ranking match/finalizer and cancel-race tests passed as the complementary family matrix. No inference or upstream code. |
| M8-CAN-05 | **Adopted local correctness fix.** [`execute_finalize`](../../app/app/engine_tasks_node.py) passes its claimed task to [`_commit_leased_report_publication`](../../app/app/report_render.py), which reuses the existing lease/attempt/run guard under one SQLite write transaction. The transaction saves report and facts, appends report/completed events, marks the run completed and enqueues only an opted-in email. The best-effort Markdown file is written after commit; the database text remains authoritative. [`reconcile_interrupted_runs`](../../app/app/store/runs_reconcile.py) settles only a leased finalizer on a completed run with a persisted report after a crash-before-ack. | Code commit `daa048cf`. An owned cancellation after `safety.final` was RED on old code: stale finalize reversed cancellation and exposed report, facts, share and email task. It now raises lease loss with none of those effects. Leased normal and crash-before-ack controls verify API report/Markdown, facts, ordered single events, one email task, 409 late cancel and restart persistence. 35 affected app tests, four source-size tests, lint/type checks and independent review passed. No model or upstream code; full M8 release remains open. |
| M8-CAN-05b | **Open adjacent final-stage safety gap.** [`_block_for_empty_leaderboard`](../../app/app/report_render.py) writes a readiness decision, `BLOCKED` status and event without a finalize lease guard. Final safety can also append a late allow/redact event after cancellation during screening. | Test a cancelled, stale finalizer through both branches and require no post-cancel readiness/allow/redact effects. Preserve valid block and redaction decisions and their owner-visible audit trail. Keep this separate from the successful-publication transaction in M8-CAN-05. No model call. |
| M8-PAUSE-08e | **Adopted local pause and recovery correction.** [`execute_finalize`](../../app/app/engine_tasks_node.py) previously checked pause before final drain, then overwrote a completed pause with `SYNTHESIZING`; an early pause read could also race with `/resume`. | Code commit `cdc5fd19` makes both checkpoint decisions lease-fenced and atomic with current run status. Owned API tests cover in-drain pause, cancel, early resume, checkpoint/restart, explicit resumed publication, metrics and event order. No model call; final M8 release remains open. |
| M8-SSE-03 | **Already covered.** [`runs_events`](../../app/app/runs_events.py) replays an append-only per-run SQLite sequence under owner authorization, then tails it; [`use_run_stream`](../../app/frontend/src/hooks/use_run_stream.ts) reconnects and deduplicates by sequence. A 2,048-event retention gap and `Last-Event-ID` recovery are unnecessary with retained history; cursor query is supported. | Existing server and hook tests cover replay, ownership, reconnect and duplicate suppression. The only potential cost is full-history replay after reconnect; no demonstrated lost event or unacceptable load warrants changing the protocol. No code or model call. |
| M8-DEC-04 | **Already covered for the authorized flow; local grant scopes are outside scope.** [`resolve_safety_decision`](../../app/app/store/records_safety.py) conditionally resolves a held decision once, records actor/time, and the owned [`adjudicate` route](../../app/app/runs_collections.py) advances the durable lifecycle. OpenScience's in-memory continuation cannot provide our restart guarantee or multi-tenant ownership. | [`test_run_safety_adjudication.py`](../../app/tests/test_run_safety_adjudication.py) covers single-use and wrong-identity decisions; [`test_safety_hold_resume.py`](../../app/tests/test_safety_hold_resume.py) covers the parked task. No setup or inference needed. |
| M8-ART-05 | **Already covered for scientific provenance.** Current hypothesis parent lineage, claim-to-evidence rows, source spans, append-only events and published report link the displayed result to its evidence. OpenScience's separately saved workspace-file artifact is a different local-workbench product. | Retaining report snapshots internally while publishing only the latest is deliberate: an older snapshot may predate a safety or contradiction decision. No concrete current regeneration/inspection case justified exposing outdated versions. Existing report and provenance tests and UI flows are the applicable boundary; no second store, graph, dependency or model call. |

An upstream metadata catalog cannot substitute for those checks. | No user-facing model chooser exists to consume model-level catalog fields. Avoid catalog fetches and managed paid routes; model capability remains an operational qualification rather than a new runtime or UI mode. No code or model call. |
| M8-LLM-07 | **Open, transferred to M11-LLM-02 for cross-source resolution.** Engine calls count a request before dispatch and cache successful completions, but a lost response can leave the outcome unknown; the durable worker currently retries `LLMTimeoutError`. OpenScience's idempotent replay works only through its managed gateway, not arbitrary direct providers or BYOK. Adding a header here would make an unsupported exactly-once claim. | First reproduce provider-native timeout classification and the durable ambiguous-timeout retry in offline tests. A safe choice needs a provider-backed receipt or a durable unknown-outcome state with an explicit recovery path; blanket no-retry harms transient free-service recovery, while auto-replay may charge BYOK users. No live inference until a zero-cost path is proven. Keep this candidate open; lack of a compatible gateway is not evidence for rejection. |

This comparison adopts two **external techniques** as local reliability fixes; it does not infer that Google implemented either one. Every other decision preserves the existing FastAPI/React/LangGraph/SQLite and owner-scoped report workflow. No upstream code is copied. Release measurements, changed-file attribution, and deployed behavior remain to be recorded.

## M8-CAN-02 implementation evidence

**Reuse:** independently implemented the transaction-fencing principle; no OpenScience source code or dependency was copied. [`_assert_task_commit_allowed`](../../app/app/engine_tasks_support.py) reads the current run and task row after acquiring SQLite's immediate write lock. It requires a live lease with the same worker and attempt number and a nonterminal run before any checkpoint, metrics, steering acknowledgement or successor writes. The guard is called by node, exact-successor and paused-checkpoint transactions, the direct generation-plan transaction, and the shared review/verification/reflection fan-out transaction. A legitimate paused checkpoint remains permitted; normal successor work after a late pause is a separate M8-PAUSE-04 item.

**Red/green boundary:** an owned API cancellation after `execute_node_task`'s final run-status read but before its commit previously wrote checkpoint 2 and queued `engine.node.generate`; the test failed because the expected lease-loss exception was not raised. The equivalent review fan-out interleaving left both an item and aggregate queued. A same-worker expired lease re-claim advanced the database attempt to 2 while a stale attempt-1 object still passed a worker-name-only guard; this was red before attempt fencing. All three scenarios now roll back or refuse their writes. The coordinator reran `tests/test_engine_tasks_cancel_commit.py`, `test_engine_tasks.py`, `test_engine_tasks_fanout.py`, `test_engine_tasks_fanout_verification.py`, `test_engine_tasks_generation.py`, and `test_task_worker_resume.py`: **28 passed**. Focused Ruff format/check and mypy passed. Independent read-only review found no defect in the edited commit paths and identified the separate, recorded initial/final lifecycle and pause windows. This is local correctness evidence; full release checks and deployed behavior remain open.

## M8-PAUSE-08a implementation evidence

**Root cause and choice:** [`pause_run`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py) atomically parks then-queued tasks and marks the run PAUSED, but a leased fan-out scheduler or aggregate can commit new queued rows afterward. Suppressing each family commit would risk losing its already-computed result. The minimal shared correction instead makes [`claim_task`](../../app/app/store/tasks.py) reject engine rows belonging to a PAUSED run inside its write transaction; advisory claim and cohort probes agree without writing on idle ticks, while live sibling leases remain visible. Queued post-pause rows remain durable for explicit resume. This is a **local design choice** informed by OpenScience's admission/replay discipline, not evidence of Google behavior; no upstream code was copied.

**Resume correctness:** code commit `9aa8fbc1` also makes unpause, latest-checkpoint/task discovery, expired-writer revival and fallback enqueue one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. The discovery uses checkpoint successor, producer and fan-out provenance so post-pause generation/review children and exact ranking rows are reused rather than outrun by a priority-100 orchestrator fallback. A paused checkpoint's still-leased writer cannot stand in for its deliberately absent successor; an expired, spent writer is revived before its dependent child. A deterministic race test failed when the transaction was temporarily replaced with a non-locking connection and passed when restored.

**Red/green boundary and limits:** tests first observed a claim during PAUSED, wrong fan-out resume, lost paused successor, a child blocked behind a spent lease, an expired paused lease keeping a cohort active, and checkpoint/task snapshot mismatch. HTTP pause/resume tests cover generation's plan checkpoint, the shared review/verification/reflection fan-out scheduler and a verification aggregate; the latter retains claim evidence, articles, metrics and its completion event. Coordinator reran 44 focused app tests and 30 neighboring node/ranking/lifecycle/cancel tests; direct function/file-size tests passed 4/4, focused mypy and Ruff passed, and independent semantic review found no remaining 08a defect. M8-PAUSE-08b/c/d retain pre-checkpoint bootstrap, realistic ranking and whole-run acceptance; full M8 release checks and deployment remain open. No model inference or paid tool was used.

## M8-PAUSE-08b implementation evidence

**Root cause and choice:** [`execute_bootstrap`](../../app/app/engine_tasks.py) previously acted on a PAUSED status snapshot before its checkpoint transaction. A concurrent `/resume` could change the run to QUEUED, yet bootstrap would still commit a paused checkpoint without a successor. Conversely, `/pause` could return before the first checkpoint while its sole bootstrap stayed leased; [`_is_resumable`](../../app/app/runs_lifecycle.py) returned false, so `/resume` returned 409. Code commit `69df1a79` uses the existing pause-aware checkpoint/successor transaction and recognizes a pre-checkpoint bootstrap lease as durable work. This is a **local design choice** informed by OpenScience's admission/replay discipline, not Google-backed behavior; no upstream code was copied.

**Recovery boundary:** An expired bootstrap lease with exhausted attempts can be marked FAILED by cohort abandonment while its run remains PAUSED. Explicit resume now recognizes that precise shape using the store's canonical dead-lease error and exhausted attempt count, then revives the original idempotency row in the resume transaction. A live lease remains owned, and a permanent failure at the same attempt count is not revived. The pre-checkpoint true-resume path preserves intake safety decisions and events. Cancelled runs and foreign owners remain excluded. The separate concurrent cancellation-after-resume-admission race remains M8-PAUSE-08d.

**Red/green and release evidence:** Red owned API/task tests showed `/resume` 409 for the live and abandoned pre-checkpoint bootstrap, a stale PAUSED read committing the wrong checkpoint after resume, and an initially overbroad revival of a permanent failure. The corrected tests plus neighboring admission, worker, queue and engine cases passed: 50 app tests; app-wide mypy passed across 509 files; direct file/function size tests passed 4/4; focused Ruff check/format and diff check passed. Two independent semantic reviews identified the abandonment and permanent-failure distinctions before the final narrowed implementation passed review. No model inference, paid service, PR or deployment occurred; ranking, whole-run pause acceptance and M8 release verification remain open.

A realistic fake-judge/finalizer run showed the shared M8-PAUSE-08a claim fence keeps that successor unclaimable while PAUSED, and the resume transaction reuses the exact checkpoint-linked match or orchestrator task. A separate paused-checkpoint mechanism would duplicate this working recovery path and require reconstructing match-specific successor inputs, so the queued-row design was retained. Elo and matchup details live in workflow checkpoints during the tournament; relational match rows are published by the normal final drain, not by each wave. This is a **local design choice**, not evidence of Google's internal implementation.

## M8-PAUSE-08d1 implementation evidence

**Defect and boundary:** An owned `/resume` could observe PAUSED, then lose to `/cancel` before writing QUEUED, a `resuming` event and claimable successor. The red API test observed exactly that reversal. A status comparison alone missed PAUSED → CANCELLED → explicit resume → PAUSED (ABA). The same race applied to startup recovery and approved safety-hold release; a rejected safety hold could overwrite cancellation with BLOCKED. These are **local correctness requirements** informed by OpenScience's admission discipline, not evidence of Google's private implementation.

**Correction:** Code commit `f2a52890` reads status and the latest status/lifecycle event sequence in one snapshot. Inside one SQLite write transaction it compares both, prepares legacy or engine resume state, writes QUEUED and `resuming`, and revives or enqueues the exact task. A cancel committed first yields 409 with no later resume effects; a cancel waiting behind the resume transaction revokes its queued work afterward. Explicit later resume of an already-cancelled checkpointed run remains supported. Startup and safety-adjudication callers pass their observed admission token; safety rejection conditionally blocks only the unchanged held run. Legacy cleanup retains status/lifecycle audit events alongside scientist outcomes and first writes a retained lifecycle reset marker above the old event high-water mark. Thus neither the admission revision nor the SSE sequence can recycle after generated logs and the legacy checkpoint are cleared. No upstream code or dependency was copied.

**Red/green evidence and limits:** Owned API/task barriers covered both transaction orders, full ABA for engine and legacy checkpoints, losing legacy cleanup, startup admission, safety rejection, ownership, ordinary resume and ordered events without inference. A corrected legacy ABA fixture seeded status sequence 1, pause sequence 2 and a later generated event; simulated old cleanup made the stale resume return 200 at its queue barrier, while the final code returns 409 and the resumed event sequence exceeds the old high-water mark. Coordinator reran 72 affected app tests, app-wide mypy across 513 files, focused Ruff check/format, four direct size gates and `git diff --check`, all passing. Independent review found both the legacy alias and event-continuity issue before correction. M8-PAUSE-08d2/d3, final-publication cancellation, request receipts, full release checks and deployment remain open.

**Local correctness gap and acceptance:** [`test_report_final_safety_cancel.py`](../../app/tests/test_report_final_safety_cancel.py) uses an owned API run and a real claimed `engine.finalize` row. A cancellation that commits first leaves no late audit or status write; an earlier committed safety audit remains visible even if cancellation prevents publication. The old publication cancellation test now injects cancellation after final safety commits, at the publication boundary, because the task-aware path returns persisted event stubs rather than re-emitting them. ## M8-PAUSE-08e final-drain pause and early-resume races

**Local gap and acceptance:** The owner could receive a successful /pause while an already-leased finalizer's drain was still running. The old finalizer then wrote SYNTHESIZING unconditionally, emitted stages and published a report. The red owned API test observed that PAUSED-to-completed reversal. A separate red race let /resume return queued after the early finalizer read PAUSED but before its checkpoint write; the old path still returned paused and wrote a stale checkpoint. These are local lifecycle correctness findings informed by OpenScience's admission discipline, not Google-backed behavior or upstream code reuse.

**Adopted mechanism:** Code commit cdc5fd19 moves the post-drain status decision into one short SQLite transaction with the finalizer lease check. If pause won, it clears replayable drain artifacts, saves an engine_task_paused checkpoint against the original checkpoint sequence with engine.finalize as successor, preserves drain-adjusted metrics, and returns before stages/report. If finalization won, it saves metrics, enters SYNTHESIZING and appends the three ordered stage-progress events in the same transaction; a later /pause is no longer admitted, while a later /cancel cannot be followed by stale stages or publication. The early pause path now rechecks PAUSED atomically with checkpoint creation, so a concurrent resume that wins does not strand the run. Workflow serialization and provider work remain outside the write lock. A true retry may emit another attempt's stage-progress events, as before; these are append-only progress signals and citation.grounding refreshes the UI collection, while report publication has its own idempotent lease-fenced commit.

**Evidence and limits:** [test_report_pause_drain_acceptance.py](../../app/tests/test_report_pause_drain_acceptance.py) covers pause during the real drain wrapper, persisted artifact cleanup, no report before explicit resume, paused checkpoint/restart reconciliation, resumed report, metrics, cancellation during drain and after stage commit, early resume, and authenticated event order. The cancellation-during-drain case was red under the legacy unconditional transition and green under the fenced path. ## M8-SAF-07 bootstrap intake audit and redaction fence

**Gap and adoption:** A red owner API/bootstrap test cancelled a task while intake screening was in flight; the old gate then wrote `safety.intake` and redacted the persisted goal after cancellation. An expired lease could likewise accept an `allow` verdict. [`_screen_bootstrap_intake`](../../app/app/engine_tasks_inputs.py) now supplies its claimed task to the existing task-bound gate, which checks [`bootstrap_task_lease_matches`](../../app/app/store/runs_bootstrap.py) inside the same SQLite write transaction as the audit decision, optional [`redact_run_goal`](../../app/app/store/runs.py), safety event, and block/hold status event. Stale work raises lease loss before any effect. The final-stage path still uses its existing claimed-finalizer guard. This independently implements a local correctness technique; no OpenScience code or new runtime was imported.

**Verification:** [`test_safety_intake_redaction.py`](../../app/tests/test_safety_intake_redaction.py) covers cancelled redaction, expired-lease allow, owner-visible safety provenance, scrubbed report content and event order. Independent review identified older cancellation/reassignment block/hold tests in [`test_engine_tasks_cancel_admission.py`](../../app/tests/test_engine_tasks_cancel_admission.py) that expected stale work to return a normal outcome; all four failed under the new contract before those expectations were corrected to require lease loss and no decision/event. The 25 affected tests, four direct size tests, Ruff/format, focused mypy and diff checks pass. No model inference or paid service was used. Final M8 release checks and deployment remain open.
